newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Stop BA, American link-up, Virgin to tell EU.
newsitem.headline: Stop BA, American link-up, Virgin to tell EU.

text.p: The European Commission should block the alliance between British Airways and AMR Corp's American Airlines, the chairman of Virgin Airlines, Richard Branson, told Reuters on Monday.

Branson, in Brussels to attend a hearing of parties interested in the transatlantic air deal, said there were practically no conditions that the Commission or the British authorities could impose to compensate for the elimination of competition.
"We are urging the Commission to stop it," Branson said by telephone.
"The only way you could redresss the balance is, at least, to have another carrier with the same number of slots and (flight) frequencies," he added.

But this was unlikely to happen. Together BA and American will control nearly 80 percent of the routes between Britain and the United States, he said. Virgin would come second with 10 percent of the traffic followed by United Airlines with a nine percent share.
Britain's Office of Fair Trading proposed in December clearing the deal provided the two airlines gave up 168 weekly landing and taking off slots at London Heathrow airport.
Branson supported the Commission's view, based on existing EU civil aviation rules, that if slots were to be given up they should not be sold.
"Slots should not be allowed to be sold. They should be there for the European Community or national governments to allocate for the benefit of consumers," he said.

The hearing, which started on Monday and will continue on Tuesday, was organised by the Commission to give all interested parties the opportunity to comment on the controversial alliance. BA and American defended their alliance on Monday.
Branson, who will speak on Tuesday, said nearly all U.S. carriers were present, whereas European airlines were represented by their governments.
U.S. companies included United Airlines, Delta Airlines, USAir and Continental, Branson and a Commission source said.
